reviewKind: FIRST English independent textual review; not a restoration or a historical Chinese approval.
summary: The new English text preserves the source's substantive science while replacing unlimited historical claims with appropriate qualifications. Three explanation gaps prevent an eight-year-old independent reader from understanding the first law, heat capacity, and those qualifications without outside help. Retain the substantive concepts and technical names; add brief explanations, not an infantilized rewrite.

science.observation: Thermodynamics is correctly presented as a macroscopic, phenomenological description rather than as unreliable science. Kinetic theory relates bulk behavior to particle motion and interactions; Newtonian mechanics is qualified as a classical approximation. Statistical mechanics is related to, but not indiscriminately equated with, every kinetic model. The first law includes heat and work in energy conservation, without treating heat as a substance or claiming that all energy transfer raises temperature. Material properties can require experiments, the laws alone do not determine each body's heat capacity, and solid/liquid microscopic calculations can be complicated. The complementary approaches retain their model assumptions and experimental basis rather than unlimited correctness or complete explanation of all microscopic phenomena.

textualSourceFidelity.observation: The source's nineteenth-century account remains explicitly attributed to the textbook, including its second-half and end-of-century statements, rather than presented as a newly established exact chronology. Instrumental measurements, macroscopic examples, first-law energy conservation, particle theory, experimental support, thermodynamic usefulness, measured heat capacities, solid/liquid complexity, complementary theories and the course's next topic are all retained. Modern qualifications do not excise these concepts. The closing passage attributes earlier-school review to the original course and does not assume the present eight-year-old reader has taken it.

readability.observation: Short paragraphs help, and macroscopic and phenomenological are given some explanation. However, the first-law passage still assumes understanding of system, surroundings, heat and work; heat capacity is named but not explained; and several applicability caveats replace absolute claims with unexplained abstract terminology. The findings below identify the required local repairs.

findings.title: Explain the first-law energy account rather than only naming it
findings.excerpt: Energy is accounted for in the system and its exchanges with its surroundings.
findings.problem: Neither system nor surroundings is defined, and including heat and work does not explain what either transfer means. An independent eight-year-old can repeat the sentence without understanding what is being counted or how conservation applies. This is a missing explanation, not a finding that the present first-law statement is scientifically false.
findings.action: Within this prose object, explain that the system is the body or material chosen for study and the surroundings are what is outside it. Briefly distinguish energy transferred because of a temperature difference (heat) from energy transferred by mechanical action (work). State positively that, when no material enters or leaves the chosen system, its change in stored energy is the net energy transferred to it. A concise water/body example is sufficient; no equation, invented measurement or new figure is needed.
findings.preserve: Keep energy conservation, transfers and conversions, the first-law name, and both heat and work. Do not imply that heat or work is a stored substance, or that every energy transfer changes temperature.

findings.title: Define the material quantity that motivates the comparison
findings.excerpt: A thermodynamic calculation often needs material properties such as heat capacity.
findings.problem: Heat capacity is the passage's only concrete example of information needed beyond the thermodynamic laws, but the text never explains what it describes. Consequently the next paragraph's such properties has no understandable physical referent for a reader encountering this term for the first time.
findings.action: Add a short explanation that a body's heat capacity describes how much energy is needed to raise that body's temperature by one degree under stated conditions, without a change of phase. Then retain the experimental-measurement sentence and the statement that thermodynamic laws alone do not supply this quantity. Keep the following statistical-mechanics and solid/liquid discussion connected to that defined example.
findings.preserve: Do not replace heat capacity with specific heat per unit mass, claim it is identical for all bodies or conditions, or remove the experimental and microscopic-model comparison.

findings.title: Make the model-applicability qualifications intelligible
excerpts: Ordinary bulk thermodynamics also requires suitable conditions, such as sufficiently well-defined system properties.
The classical version uses Newtonian mechanics where that approximation applies.
Statistical mechanics can also provide a theoretical explanation of thermodynamic laws within the appropriate regime.
findings.problem: These scientifically appropriate limits depend on bulk, well-defined system properties, approximation and regime without explaining what conditions are being limited. The many particles definition does not explain why a particular description might fail. The resulting cautions are not independently usable explanations for the assigned reader.
findings.action: Introduce model as a simplified description that works when its assumptions fit the body and conditions being studied. Explain the macroscopic qualifier with a concrete property such as whether one temperature can adequately describe the body; do not imply that Earth or every illustrated object necessarily has one uniform temperature. Describe the classical assumption as treating particle motion with Newton's laws, and replace appropriate regime with plain wording tied to the model's assumptions and conditions. Reuse that explanation for the other applicability sentences rather than adding more unexplained caveats.
findings.preserve: Retain the limits on classical particle mechanics, thermodynamic calculations and statistical explanations. Keep every macroscopic example, Figure $1$, the non-common-scale statement and the separate caption. Do not repair readability by restoring the source's unlimited all-processes or complete-molecular-explanation claims.
